items.title: Different verbs point at what they reach
items.caption: Seeing, feeling, and watching all use *i* before the second participant in these printed sentences.

cells.sm: Sā vaʻai le teine i le iʻa.
Sā matamata le tama i le pusi.
Sā alofa le tama i le teine.
Sā ʻinoʻino le teine i le ʻiole.

items.title: Want an action or want a thing
items.caption: The word *fia* stands before an action. The verb *manaʻo* points at a wanted thing with *i*.

states.label: Wanted thing
states.sm: ʻUa manaʻo le tama i le meaʻai.

items.title: Build the two-participant sentence
items.intro: Put the printed words in order. The girl-and-fish sentence accepts both orders that the chapter gives after the verb.

items.sm: Sā vaʻai le teine i le iʻa.
accept: Sā vaʻai i le iʻa le teine
items.why: The verb comes first. The chapter allows the two parts after it in either printed order.

items.sm: Sā ʻou vaʻai i le iʻa.
items.why: The preverbal pronoun keeps its middle slot, and the thing seen follows with *i*.

items.sm: Sā ia vaʻai i le pusi.
items.why: The preverbal pronoun comes before the verb, while the cat follows with *i*.

items.sm: Sā ʻou valaʻau i le uō.
items.why: The caller is in the middle slot, and the person called to follows with *i*.
